question: What are Key Audit Matters under SA 701? How does the auditor determine and communicate them, and when is a matter not communicated?
sources: SA 701 Communicating Key Audit Matters in the Independent Auditor's Report

points.label: Meaning and applicability
points.description: Matters that, in the auditor's professional judgment, were of most significance in the audit of the current period financial statements; mandatory for audits of listed entities.
points.basis: SA 701, definition and scope (audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements of listed entities)

points.label: Determining key audit matters
points.description: Select from the matters communicated with those charged with governance those requiring significant auditor attention, considering higher risks of material misstatement, significant judgments and significant events or transactions.

points.label: Communication in the auditor's report
points.description: Describe each matter in a separate 'Key Audit Matters' section, explaining why it was considered most significant and how it was addressed in the audit.
points.basis: SA 701, communicating key audit matters in a separate section of the auditor's report

points.label: Not a substitute for opinion or disclosure
points.description: Communicating key audit matters is not a substitute for a modified opinion, for a material uncertainty about going concern, or for management's disclosures.
points.basis: SA 701, relationship with modified opinions (SA 705) and material uncertainty related to going concern (SA 570)

points.label: Circumstances where a matter is not communicated
points.description: A matter is not communicated if law or regulation precludes public disclosure, or in extremely rare cases where adverse consequences of disclosure would outweigh the public interest benefits.
points.basis: SA 701, circumstances in which a matter determined to be a key audit matter is not communicated
